newsitem.title: CUBA: St Vincent, Grenadines prime minister in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: St Vincent, Grenadines prime minister in Cuba.

text.p: The prime minister of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, James Mitchell, arrived in Cuba Sunday on an official five-day visit.

The Cuban news agency Prensa Latina said the purpose of the visit is to improve bilateral relations between Cuba, the largest island of the Caribbean with a population of 11 million, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, a tiny island group in the Eastern Caribbean with a population of 115,000.
The agency said the official contacts that begin Monday will lead to the signing of agreements on cooperation between the two nations.

Mitchell was accompanied by high government officials and businessmen interested in increasing trade with Cuba. He is the third prime minister of English-speaking Caribbean islands to visit Cuba this year.
Prime Minister Keith Mitchell of Grenada visited the socialist island in April and Prime Minister Percival Patterson of Jamaica visited in May.
Both the Association of Caribbean State and the Caribbean Community (Caricom) have taken steps over the past months to strengthen their economic ties with Cuba.

During U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit to Jamaica earlier this year, leaders of several English-speaking Caribbean nations told him of their strong opposition to the Helms-Burton law that strengthens the U.S. embargo on trade with Cuba and calls for sanctions against other nations that have trade and financial ties with Fidel Castro's government.
